title: Self-move and other-move verbs
summary: Self-move verbs move the subject itself; other-move verbs move something else. Many verbs come in pairs, and their endings tell you which is which.

blocks.text: The course replaces the Western labels "intransitive" and "transitive" with **self-move** (自動詞) and **other-move** (他動詞). A **self-move** verb moves the subject itself: the door **opens**, a ball **falls**. An **other-move** verb moves something else: I **open** the door, I **drop** the ball. The two ideas overlap heavily with the Western labels, but self-move / other-move describes what Japanese really does.
Here is the whole idea in one pair. With a self-move verb the thing that moves takes **が**; with an other-move verb the thing that is moved takes **を**.
ドアが開く。 The door moves itself.
（私が）ドアを開ける。 I move the door.
Japanese has many pairs of closely related verbs, one self-move and one other-move. Often they share a kanji.
The mother and father of all verbs

**ある** (to be, to exist) is the "mother" of every self-move verb: it only looks inward. **する** (to do) is the "father" of every other-move verb: it must do something to something. That is why endings that look like them give the verb away.
**Rule 1: -す is other-move, always.** If one verb of a pair ends in す, that is the other-move one, because す is related to する. Whatever it replaces, the -す verb is the one that acts on something.
**Rule 2: -ある is self-move, always.** A verb ending in the sound -ある (あがる, とまる, はじまる) is related to ある, so it only looks inward.

**Rule 3: -める, -べる and -てる (a pair with む, ぶ or つ) is the other-move one.** When the self-move verb ends in -む, -ぶ or -つ, its partner ending in -める, -べる or -てる is the other-move verb. This also fits the first part of rule 2: 止まる is self-move, 止める is other-move.

blocks.en: My younger brother starts his homework.

blocks.text: **Rule 4: other pairs, decide by meaning.** For the remaining pairs of a -う verb and an -える verb (開く / 開ける, 売る / 売れる), the -える form is the one that gets flipped, and it can go either way. 開ける is other-move, but 売れる is self-move ("sells well"). Ask: who is moving whom?
A small note: self-move does not always mean there is no object. 従う ("obey") takes an object but moves only yourself. The rules are guides, not laws, but the pairs above cover most everyday verbs.

blocks.title: Remember
items: Self-move: the mover takes **が**. Other-move: the thing moved takes **を**.
A verb ending in **-す** is **other-move**: 出す, 落とす, 壊す.
A verb ending in **-ある** (あがる, とまる, はじまる) is **self-move**.
-める / -べる / -てる (止める, 始める) is **other-move**; for other -う / -える pairs, decide by meaning.

questions.note: 入れる (put in) is the other-move partner of 入る (go in).
起きる / 起こす; -す is other-move.
売れる / 売る.
-まる is self-move; its partner 閉める is other-move.
A self-move verb has no object: the window is the main carriage.
questions.en: The window closed because of the wind.

questions.note: An other-move verb does something to a thing: を.
が + self-move: the train stopped by itself.
questions.en: The train stopped at the station.

questions.note: を + other-move: the teacher started the class.

questions.instruction: Which pair is correctly matched (self-move / other-move)?
questions.note: Self-move first, other-move second.

options: I ran the water (did something to it)
The water came out by itself
questions.note: を + other-move 出す: someone did it.
閉める is other-move and needs を.
壊れる is self-move and takes が.

questions.prompt: 子供がおもちゃを壊した。
questions.note: Other-move: the subject acts on the toy.
閉める does something to the window.
questions.en: My little brother closed the window.

questions.instruction: Tap the verb that moves by itself
questions.note: 落ちる is self-move.
questions.en: The paper fell because of the wind.

questions.note: 開ける is other-move.
questions.en: My older sister opened the window.

questions.instruction: Tap the thing being acted on
questions.note: The を word is what the other-move verb acts on.

questions.prompt: The cup fell off the table.
questions.note: Self-move 落ちる takes が.
questions.en: The cup fell off the table.

questions.prompt: My little brother broke the toy.
questions.note: Other-move 壊す takes を.
questions.en: My little brother broke the toy.

questions.note: Self-move 始まる takes が.
Other-move 止める takes を.

questions.prompt: Verbs ending in す are usually self-move.
questions.note: -す verbs are other-move: 出す, 落とす, 消す.

questions.prompt: ある is the mother of all self-move verbs.
questions.note: ある only looks inward.

questions.instruction: Which of 上がる and 上げる is self-move?
options: 上がる (it ends in ある)
questions.note: -ある verbs are self-move.
